DID: pull-down rule off everywhere; test suite green (was 62 failing); 212 dead background jobs retired and 20 stale cash pins cleared; plumbing fixed (balance reads, false "busy" slowdowns, failed texts now logged, auditor names its failing check); 600 MB of old logs packed; the Sunday auto-build only says "merged" if it really merged; shock pause template back to your 30 s.
SAVED FOR LATER: fair-rose gate fix and bucket cap (need a book restart); clinch dashboard file (needs a clinch restart); old September fleet retire; nightly cleanup job; NASCAR launcher points-race filter; auditor repeat lines.
YOUR CALLS: CINATL sits $117 past its own backstop - I recommend letting it ride to the Sunday 8am check. Want quiet hours (10pm-7am) on monitor texts? 34 of the last 181 came overnight. No extra Sunday daytime books are planned unless you name some.

Longer version of the five ideas. Only #1 is being done now (it is the Truck fix you asked for this morning); the rest are still yours to call.

1) Sportsbook drops the race in the last hours. Bovada took the Truck race off its page from about 1:30 to 4:25 pm Friday (it lines up with qualifying) and did the same to ORLY and Cup for 2-3 hours each. The book keeps Bovada's last good odds for only 30 minutes, then goes into "no odds" mode: no price drops toward the crowd, no catch-up rows for sides that are behind, no buybacks, no checkpoints - everything waits until Bovada is back. That is why Heim and Honeycutt sat still Friday afternoon. Last night's audit flagged the same thing (its item C1) and suggested letting the safety moves run on the last good odds for about 3 hours. What I am building: before the race, keep the last good odds for up to 4 hours, let them drift toward the crowd where the crowd has moved, and keep the normal work running - price trims, buybacks, the late take, checkpoints, and catch-up rows so sides that are behind can join the crowd, all under the golden math (never under fair, book stays above 1.00). Growth posts for sides that are already fine wait for Bovada, and nothing is ever laid for a driver who never had odds, so your "never post before the sportsbook" rule stays. In-race is untouched. If a gap is still open an hour before green you get one text. Today's ORLY and Sunday's Cup need a restart with every order kept to pick it up; I will text a yes/no when it is tested.

2) Row waiting on the crowd. The arrival rule asks "will the crowd's normal flow fill this row before green?" and waits while the answer is yes. For Riggs the estimate kept saying yes for 17 hours while nothing filled. Idea: a patience cap - once a row has waited 3-4 times the normal check window with no fill, stop trusting the estimate and drop one cent toward the crowd (never under the golden-math floor). Costs a little margin on that one row, gets the contracts sold.
